newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey awards $118 mln Iran gas pipeline contract.
newsitem.headline: Turkey awards $118 mln Iran gas pipeline contract.

text.p: Turkey's state-run pipeline company Botas said on Monday it had awarded a $118 million contract to a Turkish consortium to build a section of a natural gas pipeline link with Iran.
"The Botas management board...from 14 firms decided upon the cheapest offer made by Fernas-STFA ENERKOM for $117.556 million," Botas said in a statement.
Turkey and Iran signed a $23 billion, 23-year gas supply contract last August under which a pipeline is to be constructed from the Iranian town of Tabriz to the Turkish capital Ankara.

Bids for construction of the 300-km (188-mile) stretch of the pipeline between the eastern Turkish towns of Erzurum and Dogubeyazit on the Iranian border were sought by Botas last December and bids were disclosed on February 28.
The United States has attempted to dissuade Turkey from going ahead with the Iran deal and encouraged it to seek alternative energy supplies as part of its efforts to isolate Iran.
The deal is one of several projects Turkey is undertaking with the aim of meeting energy demand that is expected to rise 12 percent a year in coming years.
Iran will build a 270-km (169-mile) pipeline from Tabriz to the Turkish border.
The pipeline will carry an initial three billion cubic metres of Iranian gas annually from 1998, to be raised in subsequent years to 10 billion cubic metres a year.
Officials have said construction work for the pipeline will be started by the two countries simultaneously on the common border in April.
